# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 6 (Bi-Vb Pc6)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc6
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 6
**Title (English, from literature):** Attending on a monk
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 6 (entitled *Upatiṭṭhana*) is a monastic rule of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka that forbids a fully ordained nun from attending upon a monk while he is taking a meal [Hüsken 1997]. In the canonical origin story, a nun attends upon a monk—identified as her former husband—while he eats soft food, standing nearby fanning him with one hand and holding a drinking vessel with the other [Hüsken 1997]. The text specifies non-offence clauses (*anāpatti*, Vin IV 264), establishing that no transgression occurs if the food or drink is merely handed over, arranged to be given indirectly, or if an unordained person (such as a female novice, *sāmaṇerī*) is directed to attend on the monk, a distinction discussed also in the commentary *Samantapāsādikā* [Hüsken 1997]. Modern scholarship observes that this rule served both to prevent newly ordained nuns from falling back into subservient domestic roles and to protect nuns against improper demands from monks [Hüsken 1997].
